content:
sana: Heads-up — nightly evals flagged a bunch of timeouts on the quantized-inference runs (int4). Jobs appear to hang in the sampling loop for ~8-12min before the test harness kills them. @mike did you notice this too? :eyes:

mike: yeah saw ~4 failures last night. stack traces empty, process present but 0% CPU and GPU utilization. looks like it gets stuck inside the worker pool during sampling.

eva: can you paste the minimal harness command you run for the nightly?

mike: here's the command we run for the failing jobs:

```
python -m eval_harness --model redwood/open-4q --quantize int4 --promptset nightly_regressions --workers 6 --seed 42 --max-tokens 128
```

mike: attaching the last lines from the job log: 

```
[2026-03-04 03:12:47] INFO: started sampling job id=nv_eval_1123
[2026-03-04 03:12:55] DEBUG: spawned worker pid=32145
[2026-03-04 03:13:05] DEBUG: worker(32145) entered sampling loop
...no further logs for 8m...
[2026-03-04 03:21:05] ERROR: timeout after 480s
```

mike: strace on the stuck worker shows it sitting in futex wait and occasional ioctl to /dev/nvidiactl but no memcpy_s or kernel work.

jordan: two quick hypotheses: (1) CUDA context inherited across fork + mmap/tokenizer cache causing a deadlock, (2) worker start method (fork) + open file descriptors for tokenizer mmap -> race. we've seen similar with tokenizers that use shared mmap pages.

sana: relevant change — last week I merged the parallel-sampling pool into the harness to speed nightly runs (PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/523). It uses multiprocessing.Pool with default start method. I didn't expect CUDA to be involved there.

ops-alex: which pool is this running on? dedicated-ci-gpu or hosted?

sana: dedicated-ci-gpu pool (pools/ci/dedicated/gpu-small).

eva: quick repro suggestion: run the harness locally with the same flags and 4 workers, then try different start methods. e.g.

```
import multiprocessing
multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn')
# then import torch and initialize model
```

mike: I tried spawn locally this morning and could not reproduce the hang; with fork the worker sometimes hung. With spawn it's stable.

jordan: that strongly points at CUDA context + fork semantics. When a process forks after a CUDA context is created in the parent, the child may hang on driver calls. Two short fixes: ensure no CUDA context in parent before forking, or switch to 'spawn' start method for worker pool, or move tokenizer mmap to worker init after spawn.

sana: tokenizer mmap — we do cache tokenizers at module import time for speed; that means parent opens mmap before pool.spawn/fork. If parent has created CUDA context (e.g. model loaded earlier) and then forks, that's the bad combo.

mike: reproducer I used (simplified):

```
# parent
model = load_model('open-4q', quantize='int4')  # initializes CUDA
tokenizer = TokenizerCache.get()
p = multiprocessing.Pool(4)
p.map(sample_fn, tasks)
```

Child ends up blocking inside torch.cuda._lazy_init calls.

jordan: proposed patch: in eval_harness main, set multiprocessing.set_start_method('spawn') as early as possible OR defer model.cuda() until after worker creation (i.e., initialize model inside workers). Also for tokenizer: avoid creating mmap until inside worker or reopen with O_CLOEXEC to avoid sharing FD across fork.

sana: okay i'll open a small patch to set start_method('spawn') early in the harness and add a canary nightly with reduced workers to confirm.

ci-bot: [auto] created canary job nv_eval_canary/1769012345-quant-freeze-patch (workers=3, branch=fix/multiproc-spawn).

mike: ran the canary locally with the patch — 10 runs in a row, no hang.

ops-alex: I'll keep an eye on the dedicated pool, but switching to spawn has minor perf overhead for worker startup. that's acceptable for nightly if it fixes hangs.

sana: pushed PR https://git.company/repo/pull/531 — set_start_method('spawn') + lazy tokenizer reopen. Scheduling canary on CI now.

ci-bot: [auto] canary nv_eval_canary/1769012345 finished: status=SUCCESS, failures=0, duration=16m.

mike: canary green :thumbsup: Looks like spawn + lazy tokenizer fixed the deadlock.

jordan: follow-ups: (1) add a unit test that runs a tiny quantized sample with multiprocessing on CI, (2) add docs in devex about 'don't create CUDA contexts before forking'.

sana: filing follow-ups. thanks all.

mike: extra note — we should audit other long-lived processes (deploy agents, sidecars) that might import tokenizers at startup.

sana: noted, adding to postmortem. :eyes:
